---
title: "Preliminary Simulation: Data Generation and Processing"
output: html_document
---

This file shows the data structure used in the Gaussian simulation and processes the saved results. The simulated observations are generated by `glmtrans`; no outside real-data files are used for these simulations. The full experiment is in `02_GaussianSimulation.R`.

## 1. Load packages and simulation functions

```{r}
source("00_requirements.R")
source("01_SimulationFunctions.R")
```

## 2. Generate one example of the simulated data

These settings match the first repetition of the simulation with `h = 1` and `Ka = 0`. The source and target observations are generated from the package's built-in model.

```{r}
K = 6
p = 500
s = 10
n_target = 100
n_source = 100

set.seed(1001)
target = generate_target(n_target, K, p, s)
example_test = generate_target(1000, K, p, s)

set.seed(3100)
sources = generate_sources(h = 1, K = K, Ka = 0,
                           n_source = n_source, p = p, s = s)

print(dim(target$x))
print(length(target$y))
print(length(sources))
print(dim(sources[[1]]$x))
```

## 3. Check and prepare the generated predictors and responses

The same predictor columns are used in the target and source datasets. The data are generated directly as numerical matrices, so no imputation or gene-expression cleaning is needed for this simulation.

```{r}
# Check dimensions and missing data.
stopifnot(ncol(target$x) == p)
stopifnot(length(target$y) == nrow(target$x))
stopifnot(all(sapply(sources, function(z) ncol(z$x) == p)))

missing_target = sum(is.na(target$x)) + sum(is.na(target$y))
missing_sources = sum(sapply(sources, function(z) sum(is.na(z$x)) + sum(is.na(z$y))))

print(data.frame(dataset = c("Target", "All six sources"),
                 missing_values = c(missing_target, missing_sources)))

# Make a small sample of the analysis data with a common set of predictors.
target_table = data.frame(dataset = "target", y = target$y, target$x)
source1_table = data.frame(dataset = "source_1", y = sources[[1]]$y, sources[[1]]$x)
print(head(target_table[, 1:6]))
print(head(source1_table[, 1:6]))
```

## 4. Read and process the saved simulation results

These four CSV files are saved by `02_GaussianSimulation.R`. Each row in `simulation_results.csv` is the prediction error for one method, repetition, and parameter setting. `source_detection.csv` records one source decision per repetition and setting.

```{r}
results = read.csv("results/simulation_results.csv")
detection = read.csv("results/source_detection.csv")

# Check for missing results before calculating averages.
print(colSums(is.na(results)))
print(colSums(is.na(detection)))
results = results[complete.cases(results), ]
detection = detection[complete.cases(detection), ]

# Average prediction errors across ten repetitions per setting.
average_results = aggregate(cbind(mse, mae) ~ h + Ka + method,
                            data = results, FUN = mean)
print(head(average_results))

# Proportion of times a transferable or non-transferable source was selected.
selection_rates = aggregate(selected ~ h + Ka + transferable,
                            data = detection, FUN = mean)
print(head(selection_rates))
```

## 5. Draw the two figures from the processed data

```{r fig.width=12, fig.height=5}
plot_mse = ggplot(average_results,
                  aes(x = Ka, y = mse, color = method, group = method)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) + geom_point(size = 2) +
  facet_wrap(~ h, labeller = label_both) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 0:6) +
  labs(title = "Prediction error by number of transferable sources",
       x = "Number of transferable sources (out of 6)",
       y = "Average test MSE", color = "Method") +
  theme_minimal()
print(plot_mse)
```

```{r fig.width=12, fig.height=5}
plot_detection = ggplot(selection_rates,
  aes(x = Ka, y = selected,
      color = factor(transferable, levels = c(FALSE, TRUE),
                     labels = c("Not transferable", "Transferable")),
      group = transferable)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) + geom_point(size = 2) +
  facet_wrap(~ h, labeller = label_both) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 0:6) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 1)) +
  labs(title = "How often automatic Trans-GLM selects sources",
       x = "Number of transferable sources (out of 6)",
       y = "Average selection rate", color = "Source type") +
  theme_minimal()
print(plot_detection)
```

The future analysis will match GDSC2 gemcitabine response with RNA-seq expression and cancer-type labels. The real-data preprocessing is documented separately in 20_RealData_DataProcessing.Rmd
